definition: A physical neural network is a type of artificial neural network in which an electrically adjustable material is used to emulate the function of a neural synapse or a higher-order (dendritic) neuron model.
details: "Physical" neural network is used to emphasize the reliance on physical hardware used to emulate neurons as opposed to software-based approaches. More generally the term is applicable to other artificial neural networks in which a memristor or other electrically adjustable resistance material is used to emulate a neural synapse.

explainer.lead: A physical neural network is an artificial neural network in which an electrically adjustable material emulates a neural synapse or a higher-order neuron model. It matters because it emphasizes reliance on physical hardware rather than software-based approaches.

tiers.eli5: Instead of simulating brain connections in code, it uses special materials that change their electrical resistance to act like connections.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use memristors or other electrically adjustable resistance materials to emulate synapses; a pitfall is assuming the network is software-based when the computation relies on physical hardware.
tiers.paperLevel: A physical neural network uses an electrically adjustable material to emulate a neural synapse or higher-order dendritic neuron model; the term applies to networks using memristors or other electrically adjustable resistance materials.

explainer.example: A memristor array is used as the synapse layer of a neural network, with resistance adjusted electrically.
